algorithms.name: Posterior sampling with initial designed exploration (pi^IPS_{a_1..a_d})
requires_knowledge_of: actions a_1..a_d with linearly independent features

source.label: prop:finite
source.quote: If $|\mathcal{A}|=K<\infty$ and $R_t \in [0,1]$, then for any $T\in \mathbb{N}$ \mathrm{BayesRegret}(T, \pi^{\mathrm{PS}}) \leq 2\min\{K, T\}+4\sqrt{K T(2+6\log(T))}.

results.notes: Bound uniform over priors. Posterior sampling does not use T, so anytime. Numbering inferred (first proposition is the decomposition).

source.label: prop:linear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $\sigma$, $c_1$, and $c_2$. If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ... then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) = O(d \log T \sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Derived via regret decomposition plus Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011 analysis; no formal proof given.

symbols.E_sqrt_l0: E[sqrt(||theta||_0)], prior expectation of square root of number of nonzero components of theta

results.notes: Sparse-linear bound; depends on prior through E sqrt(||theta||_0), labelled instance_dependent loosely.

symbols.r: ratio sup g' / inf g' of slopes of the link function over the feasible domain

extra_assumptions: exist a_1..a_d with sum phi(a_i)phi(a_i)^T >= lambda I

source.label: prop:generalizedLinear
source.quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=g(\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle)$ ... then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm IPS}_{a_1,\ldots,a_d}\right) = O(r d \log^{3/2} T \sqrt{T}),$ where $r=\sup_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a), \rho\rangle) / \inf_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a),\rho\rangle)$.

results.notes: Applies to modified PS with initial d designed exploration actions.

source.quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, ... then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right)\leq 1+2\sqrt{T \gamma_T \ln\left(1+\sigma^{-2}\right)^{-1} \ln\left(\frac{(T^2+1) \left| \mathcal{A}\right|} {\sqrt{2\pi}} \right)}$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Interpreted ln(1+sigma^-2)^{-1} as 1/ln(1+sigma^-2). K denotes |A|. gamma_T is maximum information gain.

symbols.C_bd: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0, C]
symbols.beta_star: confidence parameter beta*_T(F, delta, alpha) = 8 sigma^2 log(N(F,alpha,||.||_inf)/delta) + 2 alpha T (8C + sqrt(8 sigma^2 ln(4T^2/delta)))

source.label: prop: Bayesian regret bound in terms of beta
source.quote: For all $T \in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha > 0$ and $\delta \leq 1/2T$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+ \left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +4\sqrt{{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \beta^{*}_{T} \left(\mathcal{F}, \alpha, \delta \right) T}.$

results.notes: Proposition number inferred from ordering. Note argument order of beta* differs from its definition in paper (typo).

bound.expression_latex: 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T }

symbols.C_bd: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0, C]

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: For any fixed class of functions $\mathcal{F}$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T } for all $T\in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Contains an o(1) term, so effectively asymptotic in the constant.

symbols.C_bd: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0, C]

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: Further, if $\mathcal{F}$ is finite then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +8\sigma\sqrt{2{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \log\left(2\left|\mathcal{F}\right|T\right)T},$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

Consider the case of a $d$-dimensional linear model ... ${\rm dim}_E(\mathcal{F}, \epsilon) = O(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ and ${\rm dim}_K(\mathcal{F}) = O(d)$. Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} therefore yields an $O(d\sqrt{T}\log(T))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Stated in an Example specializing Proposition 10, under the Section 7 assumptions (bounded rewards, sub-Gaussian noise).

symbols.r: ratio of maximal to minimal slope of g

source.quote: Then, ${\rm dim}_K(\mathcal{F}) = O(d)$ and ${\rm dim}_E(\mathcal{F}, \epsilon) = O(r^2 d\log(r \epsilon))$ ... Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} yields an $O(rd\sqrt{T} \log (rT))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Applies to standard posterior sampling; noise assumption here is sub-Gaussian rather than bounded as in setting s3.
